questions.explanation: Ref: Knowledge. Low voltage in BS 7671 terms does not exceed 1000 V a.c. or 1500 V d.c. The option gives the a.c. limit.

questions.prompt: In the diagram below, a ring final circuit is wired in high impact PVC conduit. The number of single core cables installed in section A to B will be
questions.explanation: A ring final circuit runs out and back, so before it branches the conduit carries two line conductors, two neutrals and two circuit protective conductors. That makes six single-core cables sharing the section.

questions.prompt: A residual current device (RCD) works by

options.A: A magnetic device operating in the event of a fault between live and earth
options.B: A magnetic device operating in the event of a fault between neutral and earth
options.C: A thin element operating in the event of a fault between live and earth
options.D: A thin element operating in the event of a fault between neutral and earth

questions.explanation: Ref: 414.4.3. An RCD compares current in the live conductors and trips when leakage to earth creates an imbalance. That is represented by a magnetic sensing device operating for a live-to-earth fault.

questions.prompt: At the origin of an electrical installation, the prospective fault current must be taken into account when

options.C: Estimating the external fault loop impedance
options.D: Selecting the type of overcurrent device to be installed

questions.explanation: Ref: 424.1. Prospective fault current at the origin determines the breaking capacity and type of overcurrent protective device needed. The device must safely interrupt the worst expected fault current.

questions.prompt: Protective measures against electric shock can be achieved by automatic disconnection of the supply and in a.c. systems with additional protection by means of an rcd . Which of the following does not require this additional protection by an RCD?

options.A: Mobile equipment with a current rating not exceeding 13 A, for use outdoors
options.B: Mobile equipment with a current rating not exceeding 32 A, for use outdoors
options.C: Socket outlets for use under supervision of skilled or instructed persons
options.D: Socket outlets with a rated current not exceeding 20 A

questions.explanation: Ref: 444.1. Socket-outlets under the supervision of skilled or instructed persons can be treated differently from general-use sockets. The supervision reduces the need for the standard additional RCD protection in the option set.

questions.prompt: In a TN system, automatic disconnection of the supply in case of a fault in a 230-volt a.c. final circuit not exceeding 32 A shall have a maximum disconnection time of
questions.explanation: Ref: 434.5.2. For a TN system final circuit not exceeding 32 A at 230 V a.c., the maximum automatic-disconnection time is 0.4 seconds. This limits touch-voltage duration during faults.

questions.prompt: If a fault occurs in the HV system, and a magnitude of fault voltage of 430 volts occurs between exposed conductive parts and earth on the LV installation. What is the maximum tolerable duration of the fault?
questions.explanation: A high-voltage fault can briefly impose a stress voltage on the low-voltage installation's earthing. The higher this voltage, the shorter the time it can safely persist; at 430 V the permitted duration is 300 ms before it must be cleared.

questions.prompt: If a Line conductor of an IT system is earthed accidentally, the insulation and components rated for the Line to Neutral voltage can be temporarily stressed with a higher voltage. What value can this stress voltage reach up to?
questions.explanation: Ref: Table 41.4. In an IT system with one line accidentally earthed, unearthed conductors can be stressed by the line-to-line voltage. For a three-phase system that can be up to sqrt(3) times Uo.

questions.prompt: Class II equipment would provide

options.C: Earth fault loop impedance fault protection

questions.explanation: Ref: 544.1.1. Class II equipment uses double or reinforced insulation, so it provides both basic protection and fault protection without relying on an earth connection.

questions.prompt: Nuisance tripping from a large transformer installation can be prevented by

options.A: The use of a B type MCB
options.B: The use of a C type MCB
options.C: The use of a D type MCB

questions.explanation: Ref: 523.9. Large transformers can have high inrush current when energized. A Type D MCB tolerates higher short-duration inrush than Type B or C devices, reducing nuisance tripping.

questions.prompt: If a cable is buried in a wall less than 50mm depth and is not protected by metallic enclosures, the additional protection required is
questions.explanation: Ref: 514.9.1. A concealed cable less than 50 mm deep and not otherwise mechanically protected needs 30 mA RCD additional protection. This helps protect against shock if the cable is penetrated.

questions.prompt: The voltage drop between the origin of an installation and any load point on a low voltage circuit on a public distribution system should not exceed

options.B: 3% for lighting and 5% for other uses
options.D: 8% for lighting and 10% for other uses

questions.explanation: On a public low-voltage supply, voltage drop is limited to 3% for lighting and 5% for other uses so equipment receives adequate voltage. Lighting gets the tighter limit because lamps dim and flicker noticeably when starved of volts.

questions.prompt: At which one of the following terminations would a warning notice NOT need to be attached

options.D: An earthing terminal within a consumer unit

questions.explanation: Ref: 521.10.202. Bonding and earth-electrode terminations need warning labels because removal could make the installation unsafe. An earthing terminal inside a consumer unit is already part of the labelled enclosure and is not the same external clamp situation.

questions.prompt: Where a clamp is used for bonding purposes, a permanent label shall be fixed in a visible position with the wording
questions.explanation: Ref: 521.5.1. A bonding clamp label warns that the connection is a safety connection and must not be removed. The wording in the answer identifies it as a safety electrical connection.

questions.prompt: When designing a single circuit, correction factors are to be used and applied to the

options.A: Current carrying capacity of the cable
options.D: Nominal rating of the protective device

questions.explanation: Rating factors for grouping, ambient temperature and the like reduce a cable's effective current-carrying capacity, so the protective device's nominal rating must be coordinated with that lowered value to guarantee the conductor is properly protected against overload.

questions.prompt: When determining design current, the correction factor that is applied to a BS3036 rewireable fuse is
questions.explanation: Ref: 537.4.2.2. BS 3036 rewireable fuses need a 0.725 correction factor because their operating characteristics require extra derating. Applying it prevents the cable being overloaded before the fuse operates.

questions.prompt: A BS EN 61009 protective device is also known as a
questions.explanation: Ref: 532.1. A BS EN 61009 device combines residual-current protection with overcurrent protection. That combined device is an RCBO.

questions.prompt: A BS EN 60898 protective device is also known as a
questions.explanation: Ref: def. BS EN 60898 is the standard for domestic-type circuit-breakers. In common exam wording, that device is simply a circuit breaker or MCB.

questions.prompt: Which of the following does NOT give protection against basic contact
questions.explanation: Ref: 542.2.6. Basic contact protection is provided by insulation, barriers, enclosures or sometimes obstacles. Supplementary bonding reduces touch voltage under fault conditions, so it is not basic-contact protection.

questions.prompt: Outdoor lighting does NOT involve
questions.explanation: Ref: 533.1.2.2. Outdoor lighting in this context includes fixed lighting such as floodlighting, traffic signals and shelters. Festoon lighting is treated separately as temporary or decorative string lighting.

questions.prompt: In Great Britain the use of Combined protective and neutral (PEN) conductors is prohibited in consumers installations. One of the exceptions from this is

options.A: Where the installation is supplied by a privately owned transformer which has a metallic connection with the distributors network
options.B: Where the supply is feeding a swimming pool
options.C: Where the supply is feeding an agricultural installation
options.D: Where the supply is obtained from a private generating plant

questions.explanation: A PEN conductor depends on a sound earth back at the supply; losing it can make exposed metalwork live, so it is barred in consumers' installations. A private generating plant is a permitted exception because the user controls the whole system.

questions.prompt: Where a generating set is used as an additional source of supply in parallel with other sources, it shall be installed

options.A: On the load side of all the protective devices for the final circuits of the installation with no additional requirements
options.B: On the load side of all the protective devices to the final circuit which must be connected by plug and socket
options.C: On the supply side of all the protective devices for the final circuits of the installation with a number of additional requirements
options.D: On the supply side of all the protective devices for the final circuits of the installation with no additional requirements

questions.explanation: A generating set run in parallel with another source feeds into the installation upstream of the final-circuit protective devices, so it must be connected on the supply side rather than after them. Placing it there lets it share the load across the whole installation.

questions.prompt: Regarding auxiliary supplies to safety services, the maximum changeover time refers to

options.A: How long the safety source can supply the rated power output to the safety service
options.B: How often maintenance has to be carried out on the auxiliary supply
options.C: The frequency (in cycles per second) of the auxiliary supply feeding the safety service
options.D: The time It takes for the safety source to supply the power to the safety service, after the loss of the main power supply

questions.explanation: Ref: 544.1.1 and Table 54.8. Maximum changeover time is the time from loss of the normal supply until the safety source supplies the safety service. It is about restoration speed, not battery duration or maintenance interval.

questions.prompt: An insulation resistance test performed on a PELV installation should be capable of producing a test voltage of
questions.explanation: PELV operates at extra-low voltage, so its insulation is only stressed to a modest level. A 250V d.c. test applies a voltage suited to that band, proving the insulation without over-stressing low-voltage components; the 500V test is reserved for normal LV circuits.

questions.prompt: The paperwork that should be issued on completion of a new installation is

options.C: A schedule of test results, schedule of inspection and an electrical installation certificate

questions.explanation: Ref: 557.4.1 and Table 55.2. Completion of a new installation requires the Electrical Installation Certificate plus schedules of inspections and test results. A test sheet alone is not the complete certification package.

questions.prompt: A polarity test would be conducted to verify

options.A: Every fuse and single pole device is connected in the line conductor only
options.B: There is no breakdown of the conductor insulation
options.D: There is sufficiently low resistance to operate the protective device within its limits

questions.explanation: Ref: 559.5.1. Polarity testing confirms single-pole protective and switching devices are in the line conductor only. That prevents a circuit being apparently off while the line remains connected.

questions.prompt: A minor works certificate should be issued

options.B: When a property has been extended
options.C: Where an additional circuit is connected to an installation
options.D: Where an alteration not requiring an additional circuit is needed

questions.explanation: Ref: 643. A Minor Works Certificate is for an alteration or addition that does not involve adding a new circuit. Adding a circuit or a new installation needs fuller certification.

questions.prompt: Before conducting an insulation resistance test you should

options.B: Ensure that all lamps are removed
options.C: Ensure that the earth fault loop impedance is satisfactory
options.D: Ensure that the polarity is correct

questions.explanation: Ref: 643.3.2 and Table 64. Lamps and sensitive loads should be removed or disconnected before insulation-resistance testing so the test does not damage them or distort the reading.

questions.prompt: The minimum value of insulation resistance of a PELV circuit is
questions.explanation: Ref: 644.5. PELV circuits have the same low insulation-resistance threshold used for extra-low-voltage systems in this context. The minimum selected value is 0.5 Mohm.

questions.prompt: Self supported suspension cables within agricultural situations should be

options.A: At a height of a least 10m
options.B: At a height of a least 2m
options.C: At a height of a least 4m
options.D: At a height of a least 6m

questions.explanation: Agricultural sites involve tall machinery, vehicles and livestock, so self-supporting overhead cables must hang high enough to stay clear. A minimum height of about 6 m prevents contact or damage from passing plant and animals.

questions.prompt: If SELV or PELV is used within agricultural premises, barriers or enclosures must conform to at least
questions.explanation: Even on safe SELV/PELV systems, agricultural areas demand barriers that stop a finger reaching live parts. IPXXB specifies finger protection, guarding against accidental contact where livestock, moisture and handling make exposure more likely.

questions.prompt: In zone 1 of a swimming pool, a junction box can be installed if it is
questions.explanation: Zone 1 around a pool is a wet, high-risk area, so any junction box must be fed by SELV. With the supply limited to a safe extra-low voltage, even a fault cannot deliver a dangerous shock to a person in water.

questions.prompt: Zone 1 in a swimming pool installation is defined as the

options.B: The floor or surface expected to be occupied by persons
options.C: The horizontal plane 2m above the floor
options.D: The interior of the pool and a vertical plane 2m above the basin

questions.explanation: Zone 1 is the volume immediately surrounding the pool, bounded by the water's edge and rising to a vertical plane 2m above the basin. This captures the space a swimmer or bather can reach while wet, where shock risk is greatest.

questions.prompt: The specific IP rating for areas within zone 1 of a bathroom is
questions.explanation: Ref: 701.512.2. Bathroom zone 1 is exposed to splashing water, so equipment generally needs at least IPX4 protection. Higher ratings may be needed for water jets.

questions.prompt: In a bathroom zone 2 is defined as the

options.A: Area directly above the bath or shower
options.B: Area outside a 0.60m circumference from the bath or shower
options.C: Area within a 0.60m circumference from the bath or shower
options.D: Area within the bath or shower

questions.explanation: Ref: 709.411.4. Bathroom zone 2 is the area extending 0.60 m from the edge of the bath or shower area. The citation appears to point to marinas, so use the bathroom-zone figure to verify exact wording.

questions.prompt: In an amusement park an RCD would NOT be used to protect

options.B: Mobile equipment connected by a flexible cable

questions.explanation: Ref: 721.55.2.6 and Table 721. SELV circuits already limit shock risk by voltage and separation, so they do not need the same RCD additional protection as lighting, mobile equipment or socket circuits.

questions.prompt: On a mobile vehicle installation, a socket outlet or plug should conform to
questions.explanation: Ref: 714.1. Mobile-vehicle supply connections need robust industrial plugs and socket-outlets. BS EN 60309-2 is the relevant standard for those industrial pin-and-sleeve devices.

questions.prompt: On the d.c. side of a PV power supply system, the type of insulation that is preferable is
questions.explanation: Ref: 717.411.3.1.2. PV d.c. circuits remain energized when light is present, so stronger insulation is preferred. Class II insulation reduces reliance on earthing for fault protection.

questions.prompt: The minimum rating of socket outlets supplying a pitch on a caravan site should be
questions.explanation: Each caravan pitch must be served by a socket-outlet rated at least 16A so it can supply the typical demand of a touring caravan or motor home. A lower rating would not safely carry the expected heating, cooking and appliance load.

questions.prompt: BS EN 50085 relates to

options.D: Industrial plugs, couplers and socket outlets

questions.explanation: Ref: 715.524.201. BS EN 50085 is the product standard family for cable trunking and ducting systems. Conduit, conductors and industrial plugs are covered by different standards.

questions.prompt: The correction factor for cables installed in free air with 90°C thermosetting insulation and an ambient temperature of 40°C is
questions.explanation: Thermosetting cable is rated to 90°C, so at 40°C ambient it is still operating well below its limit and barely needs derating. The correction factor is therefore close to 1.0, giving 0.96; lower factors apply to cooler-rated PVC insulation.

questions.prompt: BS EN 60228 relates to

options.D: Industrial plugs, couplers and socket outlets

questions.explanation: Ref: Appx 4. BS EN 60228 classifies conductors of insulated cables, including conductor construction and resistance. It is not the trunking, conduit or plug standard.

questions.prompt: An insulation resistance test performed on a 230v a.c. installation should be capable of producing a test voltage of
questions.explanation: Ref: 110.1.1(vi). A 230 V insulation-resistance test uses the standard low-voltage test output of 500 V d.c. The cited reference is terse, so Table 64 is the place to verify the exact test value.

questions.prompt: What characteristics of supply should be determined before an installation design can begin?
questions.explanation: Ref: 110.2(vii). The nature of current, AC or DC, is a supply characteristic that must be known before design. It affects equipment selection, protective devices and fault behavior.

questions.prompt: A neutral can be defined as a
questions.explanation: Ref: 114.1. A neutral is a live conductor because it is part of the current-carrying system in normal operation. It is not a protective conductor.

questions.prompt: A junction box can be installed within zone 1 of a swimming pool if it is

options.C: Sealed using a suitable gasket sealant

questions.explanation: In the high-risk wet environment of pool zone 1, a junction box is only permitted when supplied by SELV. The safety extra-low voltage means a fault cannot produce a dangerous touch voltage to someone in or beside the water.

questions.prompt: Choose one of the following which does not fall under compatibility?
questions.explanation: Ref: Part 2. Compatibility concerns effects such as power factor, starting currents and transient overvoltages between equipment and supply. Continuity of service is a separate design consideration.

questions.prompt: If an electric fire has an element exposed to touch, this would increase the risk of electric shock by
questions.explanation: Ref: Part 2. An exposed heating element creates risk of direct contact with a live part in normal service. That is basic contact, not a fault-contact situation.

questions.prompt: The maximum disconnection time for a 230v a.c. circuit with a TN supply is
questions.explanation: 5s is the maximum disconnection time for distribution circuits and circuits rated above 32A on a TN system, where the fixed wiring is less likely to be in contact with a person. Final circuits up to 32A must clear faster, in 0.4s.

questions.prompt: If Ze is measured at 0.68Ω and R1+R2 is measured as 0.82Ω,the value of Zs would be
questions.explanation: Ref: 341.1. Earth fault loop impedance at a point in a circuit is Ze plus the circuit's R1+R2. Here 0.68 + 0.82 = 1.50 ohm.

questions.prompt: The maximum Zs for a 10A Type C circuit breaker protecting a standard discharge type lighting circuit is
questions.explanation: A Type C breaker needs roughly 10 times its rated current to trip instantly, so a 10A device requires about 100A of fault current. With a 230V supply, the loop impedance must stay at or below around 2.30Ω for that current to flow and disconnect in time.

questions.prompt: At the origin of an electrical installation, the prospective fault current must be taken into account when

options.C: Estimating the external fault loop impedance
options.D: Selecting the type of overcurrent device to be installed

questions.explanation: Ref: 411.3.2.4. Prospective fault current at the origin determines whether an overcurrent device can safely break the fault. Device type and breaking capacity must be chosen around that value.

questions.prompt: In a TN system, the maximum earth fault loop impedance Zs when using a 32 A , (gG) BS 88 fuse for a disconnection time of 0.4 seconds would be
questions.explanation: For a 32A BS 88 fuse to blow within 0.4s, enough fault current must flow, which sets a ceiling on loop impedance. Using the supply voltage divided by that required current gives a maximum Zs of 1.04Ω; above this the fuse would clear too slowly.

questions.prompt: In a TN system, the maximum earth fault loop impedance Zs when using a 32 A , type B circuit breaker for instantaneous operation would be
questions.explanation: A Type B breaker operates instantaneously at 5 times its rating, so 5 × 32 A = 160 A, and the maximum loop impedance is 230 V divided by 160 A, giving roughly 1.44 ohm. A lower Zs guarantees enough fault current to trip it quickly.

questions.prompt: Which of the following shall be used as a source of a FELV system?
questions.explanation: Ref: 311.1. FELV still requires a source with separation between windings so the extra-low-voltage side is not directly connected to the higher-voltage supply. Autotransformers and potentiometers do not provide that separation.

questions.prompt: Nuisance tripping from a large transformer installation can be prevented by

options.A: The use of a B type MCB
options.B: The use of a C type MCB
options.C: The use of a D type MCB

questions.explanation: Ref: 313.1. Large transformers can draw high inrush current at switch-on. A Type D MCB is less sensitive to short inrush peaks, so it reduces nuisance tripping.

questions.prompt: An installation protected by an RCD shall have a fixed notice stating

options.A: The test button should be pressed at 6 monthly intervals
options.B: The test button should be pressed monthly
options.C: The test button should be pressed occasionally
options.D: The test button should be pressed quarterly

questions.explanation: RCDs contain mechanical parts that can seize over time, so the notice instructs the user to press the integral test button quarterly to confirm the device still trips and provides protection.

questions.prompt: The maximum operating temperature of standard general purpose thermoplastic PVC cable is
questions.explanation: Ref: 418.3. Standard general-purpose thermoplastic PVC cable is rated for a maximum conductor operating temperature of 70 C. Higher temperatures require different insulation types.

questions.prompt: An unprotected cable concealed in a wall at a depth less than 50mm and installed outside the safe zones, shall be provided with

options.D: An RCD with operating current not exceeding 30mA

questions.explanation: Ref: 417.3. A cable less than 50 mm deep outside safe zones is vulnerable to nails, screws and drilling. A 30 mA RCD provides additional protection if the cable is damaged.

questions.prompt: Where a generating set is used as an additional source of supply in parallel with other sources, it shall be installed

options.A: On the load side of all the protective devices for the final circuits of the installation with no additional requirements
options.B: On the load side of all the protective devices to the final circuit which must be connected by plug and socket
options.C: On the supply side of all the protective devices for the final circuits of the installation with a number of additional requirements
options.D: On the supply side of all the protective devices for the final circuits of the installation with no additional requirements

questions.explanation: Running a generator in parallel with the public supply means both feed the installation, so it connects on the supply side ahead of the final-circuit protection, and this brings extra requirements covering matters like loss of mains and synchronising.

questions.prompt: Regarding auxiliary supplies to safety services, the maximum changeover time refers to

options.A: How long the safety source can supply the rated power output to the safety service
options.B: How often maintenance has to be carried out on the auxiliary supply
options.C: The frequency (in cycles per second) of the auxiliary supply feeding the safety service
options.D: The time It takes for the safety source to supply the power to the safety service, after the loss of the main power supply

questions.explanation: Maximum changeover time is how long it takes the safety source to supply the safety service after the normal supply fails. It is about transfer delay, not how long the standby source can run.

questions.prompt: The minimum value of insulation resistance test performed on a SELV installation is
questions.explanation: SELV operates at low voltage with no earth reference, so it is tested at 250 V DC and must read at least 0.5 megohms, confirming the insulation is sound and not leaking between conductors.

questions.prompt: When installing three phase equipment, an ADDITIONAL test that should be carried out is
questions.explanation: Ref: 433.1.1. Three-phase equipment needs phase sequence verified so motors and other phase-sensitive loads rotate or operate correctly. That is an additional check beyond ordinary polarity.

questions.prompt: Cables laid in arable or cultivated agricultural ground should be

options.D: Buried to a depth of 2.0m with mechanical protection

questions.explanation: Arable or cultivated land is regularly ploughed and worked by machinery to a significant depth, so cables must be buried at least 1.0 m down to keep them clear of any digging or tilling that could damage them.

questions.prompt: Socket outlets and hand held equipment rated up to and including 32A can have additional protection in the form of
questions.explanation: Electrical separation supplies the circuit from an isolating transformer with no earth reference, so a single fault to the surrounding metalwork cannot give a shock — making it a valid protective measure for these portable and socket loads. RCDs are the more common choice, but separation is the listed measure here.

questions.prompt: Within zone 1 of a swimming baths where water jets are used for cleaning purposes, installed electrical equipment should be rated
questions.explanation: Ref: Part 2. Water jets increase the water-ingress risk beyond ordinary splashing. Zone 1 equipment in that cleaning condition therefore needs IPX5 protection.

questions.prompt: In an area containing a bath or a shower, socket outlets must be installed
questions.explanation: Socket-outlets are kept well away from water to reduce the risk of shock when wet, so apart from limited exceptions they must sit at least 3 m horizontally from the boundary of zone 1 around a bath or shower.

questions.prompt: Floor and heating systems shall use a RCD as a means of automatic disconnection of supply with a current rating of
questions.explanation: Ref: 443.1.1. Floor and ceiling heating systems need RCD protection because heating elements can fault to surrounding conductive parts or coverings. The required residual current rating in the prompt is 30 mA.

questions.prompt: A mobile unit should have a connection between the

options.D: Vehicle chassis and main bonding terminal

questions.explanation: Ref: 422.3.9. Bonding the vehicle chassis to the main bonding terminal keeps accessible metalwork at the installation earth potential. That reduces shock risk if a fault occurs on the mobile unit.

questions.prompt: Photovoltaic equipment should always

options.A: Be considered energised on the a.c. side
options.B: Be considered energised on the d.c. side
options.C: Be used in certain listed countries only

questions.explanation: Ref: Appx 5. PV d.c. conductors can remain live whenever the array is illuminated, even if the a.c. side is isolated. That is why the d.c. side should be treated as energized.

questions.prompt: BS EN 50085 relates to

options.D: Industrial plugs, couplers and socket outlets

questions.explanation: BS EN 50085 is the product standard for cable trunking and cable ducting systems. The other options relate to conduit, plugs and cable conductors, which sit under different standards, so only trunking and ducting fits.

questions.prompt: BS 1362 relates to

options.B: 13A plugs, sockets, adaptors and connection units

questions.explanation: Ref: Table 52.1. BS 1362 is the standard for cartridge fuses used in 13 A plugs. BS 1363 covers the plugs and socket accessories themselves.

questions.prompt: BS7671 applies to
questions.explanation: Ref: 110.1(xii). BS 7671 includes photovoltaic supplies as part of its scope for electrical installations. Aircraft, distributor equipment and machine internals are excluded or covered by other rules.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 does not apply to
questions.explanation: Ref: 110.2(ii). Railway traction equipment is outside the normal scope of BS 7671. Fairgrounds and marinas are special installations covered by Part 7.

questions.prompt: Protection against electric shock under single fault conditions is
questions.explanation: Ref: Definitions. Fault protection is protection against electric shock under single-fault conditions. Basic protection is for normal conditions.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would not be defined as a live part?
questions.explanation: A live part is a conductor intended to be energised in normal use, including line and neutral conductors and the neutral bar. A PEN conductor also serves as the protective earth, so it is treated as a protective/earthed conductor rather than a live part.

questions.prompt: Every installation should be divided into circuits as necessary to avoid

options.B: Hazards to minimise inconvenience in the event of a fault

questions.explanation: Ref: 314.1(i). Circuit division reduces danger and inconvenience when a fault occurs because only the affected circuit should disconnect. It also makes isolation and maintenance more manageable.

questions.prompt: The protective measure 'automatic disconnection of supply'

options.A: Is a combination of basic and fault protection
options.B: Is a combination of under and over voltage protection
options.C: Is a method of reducing thermal effects
options.D: Is only permitted if the installation is under effective supervision

questions.explanation: Ref: 411.1(i)(ii). Automatic disconnection of supply combines basic protection with fault protection. It prevents normal contact with live parts and disconnects quickly if a fault makes exposed metalwork live.

questions.prompt: The maximum disconnection time for a 16A final circuit having Uo 230V ac on a TN system is
questions.explanation: Ref: Table 41. For a 16 A final circuit at Uo 230 V on a TN system, the table disconnection time is 0.4 seconds. This limits the duration of dangerous touch voltage.

questions.prompt: Where there is a danger of fire due to the nature of stored materials a motor with star – delta starting must be protected against excessive temperature
questions.explanation: Ref: 422.3.7. Star-delta motors can overheat in either starting or running configuration if a fault or abnormal condition occurs. Protection in both star and delta covers both operating states.

questions.prompt: In the event of failure of the provision for basic protection, additional protection may be provided by

options.C: Use of a RCD with lΔn not exceeding 30mA
options.D: Use of a time delay 100mA RCD

questions.explanation: Ref: 415.1.1. A 30 mA RCD is used as additional protection if basic protection fails. It is intended to reduce the duration of current through a person.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a method of fault protection
questions.explanation: Ref: 417.1. Placing out of reach is a basic-protection measure, not fault protection, because it only reduces access to live parts in normal conditions. Fault protection deals with exposed parts becoming live.

questions.prompt: For a TT system where disconnection in the case of earth fault is achieved by RCD, the maximum disconnection time for a general socket in a domestic kitchen is
questions.explanation: Ref: Table 41.1. TT systems normally rely on RCDs because earth fault current may be low. For the general socket circuit in the question, the maximum disconnection time is 0.2 seconds.

questions.prompt: In the event of an earth fault on the HV side of a substation, the LV installation may be affected by
questions.explanation: Ref: 422.2(ii). An HV earth fault can raise earth potentials and stress the LV installation insulation. The relevant effect is power-frequency stress voltage.

questions.prompt: Connection of extraneous conductive parts to the MET of an installation forms part of the requirements for
questions.explanation: Ref: 411.3.1.2. Main bonding of extraneous-conductive-parts to the MET is part of fault protection. It limits dangerous potential differences during earth faults.

questions.prompt: Thermoplastic PVC T&E buried less than 50mm must be protected by

options.B: Cpc the same size as the P & N

questions.explanation: Ref: 522.6.7. A thermoplastic T&E cable buried less than 50 mm deep is vulnerable to penetration. A 30 mA RCD provides additional protection where the cable lacks other accepted protection.

questions.prompt: RCD installed for protection against fire must have a rating not exceeding
questions.explanation: Ref: 532.1(i). RCDs used for fire protection are limited to 300 mA residual operating current. That level helps detect leakage faults that could cause overheating or fire.

questions.prompt: Which of the following may not be used as an earth electrode
questions.explanation: Ref: 542.2.1. Water utility supply pipes cannot be used as earth electrodes because continuity and ownership cannot be guaranteed. Purpose-made electrodes or suitable structural metalwork are acceptable options.

questions.prompt: Socket outlets with a rating not exceeding 20A for general use by ordinary persons should be
questions.explanation: Ref: 411.3.3(i) and 415.1. General-use socket-outlets up to 20 A need 30 mA RCD additional protection for ordinary persons. The RCD reduces shock risk from portable equipment and damaged leads.

questions.prompt: Lighting installations in bus shelters must be protected by
questions.explanation: Ref: 559.10.3.2 and 415.1. Bus-shelter lighting is accessible outdoors, so additional protection is required. A 30 mA RCD provides that protection.

questions.prompt: Busbar trunking systems must comply with
questions.explanation: Busbar trunking systems are factory-assembled, so they comply with the busbar trunking product standard, BS EN 60439-2. The other listed numbers cover plugs and couplers, miniature circuit breakers and cable trunking, which are different product types.

questions.prompt: The minimum acceptable value for insulation resistance in 230v supply is
questions.explanation: Ref: Table 61. For a 230 V low-voltage circuit, the minimum acceptable insulation resistance is 1.0 Mohm. Lower values indicate possible insulation deterioration or connected equipment affecting the test.

questions.prompt: Insulation resistance measured between line and neutral of a 230v domestic installation should not be less than
questions.explanation: Good insulation between live conductors should let almost no current leak across it, so on a 230 V (low voltage) circuit tested at 500 V the reading between line and neutral must be at least 1.0 megohm to be acceptable.

questions.prompt: A PV generator and array junction box must have a warning label indicating that

options.B: PV array must be cleaned regularly
options.D: Parts inside may still be live following isolation

questions.explanation: Ref: 712.537.2.2.5.1. PV d.c. equipment can remain live after isolation because the array can still generate voltage in light. The warning label alerts workers to that residual live risk.

questions.prompt: All circuits in a bathroom must have
questions.explanation: Ref: 701.411.3.3. Bathroom circuits require 30 mA RCD protection because wet conditions increase shock risk. The rule applies to all circuits serving the location.

questions.prompt: Electrical cables in Zone 1 of a fountain shall be protected against mechanical impact to
questions.explanation: Cables in zone 1 of a fountain are within reach and subject to knocks and water, so they must be protected to impact classification AG2 (medium severity) to withstand the mechanical stresses likely in that location.

questions.prompt: On agricultural premises an RCD may be used for protection against fire providing that the rating of the RCD does not exceed
questions.explanation: Ref: 705.411.1(iii). Agricultural premises have increased fire and shock risks from dust, moisture and livestock. RCD fire protection is limited to a maximum of 300 mA.

questions.prompt: Any luminaries of lighting chains used at a circus must be firmly fixed when at a height less than
questions.explanation: At a circus or fairground, low-hung lighting chains within easy reach of people could be pulled or struck, so any luminaire below 2.5 m must be firmly fixed to prevent it being dislodged and causing injury or a shock hazard.

questions.prompt: In a bathroom the protective measure of obstacles is
questions.explanation: Ref: 701.410.3.5. Obstacles are not permitted as a bathroom protective measure because wet, barefoot users cannot be expected to rely on barriers or distance. More robust measures such as ADS and RCD protection are required.

questions.prompt: Where a TN system of earthing is used in a marina the final circuits for the supply of a pleasure craft must not include
questions.explanation: Ref: 709.411.4. A PEN conductor must not be included in final circuits supplying pleasure craft in a marina. Loss of a PEN in that wet environment could make exposed metalwork dangerously live.

questions.prompt: For a 100 mA non-delay RCD to BSEN 61008 the residual test currents and maximum permitted disconnection times are
questions.explanation: A general-purpose (non-delay) RCD is tested at its rated current and at five times that value. At 100 mA it may take up to 300 ms to trip, but at 500 mA the higher fault current must disconnect it much faster, within 40 ms.

questions.prompt: Flat T & E cable clipped direct to a ceiling joist where thermal insulation exceeds 100mm thickness is installation method
questions.explanation: Ref: Table 4A2 Page 265. Flat twin-and-earth clipped to a joist with thermal insulation exceeding 100 mm is treated as installation method 101. That method reflects the reduced heat dissipation caused by insulation.
